stem: A {{m}} kg person walks {{d}} m along a {{M}} kg boat floating on still water, from one end towards the other. Ignore water resistance.
How far does the boat move relative to the water?

hints.text: No horizontal external force acts on person + boat.
So their centre of mass doesn't move.
Person moves x_p, boat moves x_b backwards, with x_p + x_b = {{d}} and m x_p = M x_b.

com-shifts-isolated.text: If the boat moved as far as the person, the centre of mass would shift. No external horizontal force acts, so it stays put.

boat-ratio.text: The person also moves relative to the water: their shift plus the boat's must add to {{d}} m. Use m ÷ (m + M).

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a length.

generic.text: m x_p = M x_b with x_p + x_b = d, so x_b = m d ÷ (m + M).

workedSolution.text: Centre of mass fixed: {{m}} x_p = {{M}} x_b, and x_p + x_b = {{d}}.
x_b = {{m}} × {{d}} ÷ ({{m}} + {{M}}) = {{ans}} m backwards (the person moves {{shore}} m forwards).

com-shifts-isolated.front: A person walks along a boat on still water. Does the centre of mass of person + boat move?
com-shifts-isolated.back: No: no external horizontal force, so the boat moves back to keep it fixed.

boat-ratio.front: Person m walks d along boat M: boat moves?

generic.front: Person walks d on a boat: boat moves?
generic.back: m d ÷ (m + M) the other way.
